Welcome to a practical guide to AI-first workflows for clinical study reports.

This book explores how organizations can move from isolated AI adoption toward
an AI-native way of working by building **AI-first workflows** across clinical
study reports. In these workflows, an AI agent performs a bounded, repeatable
first pass; people define and monitor the process, review the evidence, and
remain responsible for decisions.

The focus is not a particular model or software stack. Instead, it is on
durable principles that teams can adapt to their own technology, governance,
and operating environment.

The book is written for members of Biometrics departments in
biopharmaceutical companies who design, perform, review, or govern clinical
study reports and want to integrate AI systematically into their work.
No prior experience building AI agents is required. Familiarity with clinical
study artifacts and review processes will help readers connect the examples to
their own work.

## How to use this book {.unnumbered}

The main route is reading: begin with the Introduction (Chapters 1--4), then
follow the applied examples in order. Each example states its teaching
purpose, maturity, and prerequisites up front.

- **Main route (no setup required).** Read the chapters in order and work the
  exercises through a browser-based AI agent. You will specify requirements
  and review prepared code and results; no local R, Python, Git, or Codespaces
  setup is required on this route.
- **Technical route (optional).** If you want to run the materials yourself,
  the [day-one exercise](https://github.com/elong0527/ai4csr/tree/main/exercise/day1)
  and the rounding prototype described in Chapters 6--8 give you synthetic
  data, scripts, and expected results. Contributor setup is documented in the
  repository README.
- **Facilitator route.** Shared worksheets, completed examples, and assessment
  rubrics are linked from the exercise chapters as they become available.
